unmeasured_platforms.note: Run uname -m first to confirm arm64 or x86_64, then run this script on that machine.
The script can be rerun as-is. This task was not executed on Windows.

notes: Capture time includes browser cold start, renderFrame, and PNG screenshots. The full-frame approach does not write all 2,100 images to disk; the changed-frame approach writes unique frames to a temporary directory for encoding.

The second capture or encoding pass in two-platform rows scales the same measurement: both 9:16 outputs contain the same Chinese-language content. Reuse reduces capture passes from two to one, while encoding is still counted once per output.

Baseline encoding uses two-pass libx264 medium, with a bitrate matching the product video_encoder pixel budget. One-pass encoding calls h264_args(); if hardware encoding is unavailable, it falls back to libx264 veryfast crf 20.
720p captures are upscaled to 1080x1920 during encoding. The 1080p row compares capture only; encoding still uses 720p changed frames to avoid mixing pixel configurations in the encoding comparison.

The planned 5–5.5 minutes also includes base video rendering and quality checks. This table measures only overlay capture and this encoding pass, so it should not be treated as end-to-end processing time.
The container launches Chromium as root with --no-sandbox; the browser is chromium-headless-shell 140.0.7339.16 from the image.

docker.note: This file reports the Docker-path measurement, not a host-machine result.
